title: Safe vegetables
body: Cucumber, zucchini, lettuce, pumpkin, carrot, sweet potato. Wash thoroughly and remove leftovers after 24h to prevent mold.

title: Fruit in moderation
body: Apple, pear, banana, melon. Give 2–3 times a week — too much sugar causes obesity and shortens lifespan.

title: Calcium is critical
body: Offer cuttlebone or powdered eggshell at all times. Without calcium the shell becomes thin, cracks, and the snail stops growing.

title: Never feed
body: Citrus fruits, onion, garlic, salty or spicy food, pasta, bread. These are toxic and can kill the snail within hours.

title: Humidity 70–90%
body: Mist the terrarium twice a day with room-temperature water. Low humidity triggers hibernation.

title: Temperature 22–28°C
body: Room temperature is fine. Avoid direct sunlight — above 30°C the snail can dry out and die.

title: Substrate 5–7 cm
body: Coconut coir is ideal. Change once a month, spot-clean weekly. Never use sand — it damages the shell.

title: Shell cracks
body: Small cracks heal with enough calcium. Large breaks need isolation with high humidity until the shell hardens.

title: Taurine is essential
body: Cats cannot synthesize taurine — it must come from meat. Deficiency leads to blindness and heart disease.

title: Never feed
body: Onion, garlic, chocolate, grapes, raisins, avocado, alcohol, raw yeast dough. Some are fatal even in tiny amounts.

title: Water matters
body: Cats drink little by nature. Wet food or a running fountain reduces the risk of kidney disease.

title: Annual vaccination
body: FVRCP + rabies every 1–3 years depending on lifestyle. Even indoor cats need core vaccines.

title: Toxic houseplants
body: Lilies, dieffenbachia, philodendron, poinsettia. A few lily petals can cause acute kidney failure.

title: Window safety
body: Install screens on all windows. Falls from the 3rd floor+ cause high-rise syndrome — fractures, internal injuries.

title: Portion by weight
body: Adult dogs need 20–30 g of dry food per kg of body weight per day, split into 2 meals. Puppies eat 3–4 times a day.

title: Never feed
body: Chocolate, grapes, raisins, xylitol, onion, garlic, macadamia nuts. Xylitol is fatal at 0.1 g per kg.

title: Deworming schedule
body: Every 3–6 months even for indoor dogs. Monthly flea/tick prevention in warm seasons.

title: Watch for warning signs
body: Excessive drinking, sudden weight loss, limping, coughing at night. Any of these needs a vet visit within 48 hours.

title: Never leave in a car
body: In +25°C heat the interior reaches +50°C in 10 minutes. Heatstroke kills within 20 minutes.

title: Microchip and tag
body: Legally required in many countries. Increases return rate after escape from 20% to over 90%.

title: UVB lamp is not optional
body: Most reptiles need UVB 10–12 h/day to synthesize vitamin D3. Replace the bulb every 6 months — UVB fades.

title: Temperature gradient
body: Provide a warm basking spot (30–38°C) and a cooler side (22–25°C). Reptiles regulate body heat by moving between zones.

title: Calcium + D3
body: Dust feeder insects with calcium powder 2–3 times a week. For juveniles — every feeding.

title: Metabolic Bone Disease
body: Signs: soft jaw, curved spine, tremors. Caused by calcium/UVB deficiency. Reversible only in early stages.

title: Wash hands after handling
body: Reptiles can carry Salmonella. Never let them near food preparation areas.

title: Not just seeds
body: A seed-only diet causes fatty liver disease. Base: pellets 60–70%, fresh vegetables 20–30%, fruit 10%, seeds as treats.

title: Safe vegetables
body: Carrot, broccoli, spinach, bell pepper, zucchini. Avoid avocado, chocolate, caffeine, salty snacks.

title: Teflon fumes are deadly
body: Overheated non-stick pans release fumes that kill birds within minutes. Avoid aerosols and scented candles near the cage.

title: Sleep 10–12 hours
body: Cover the cage or move it to a dark room at night. Chronic sleep deprivation causes hormonal problems.

title: Watch the droppings
body: Change in color or consistency is often the first sign of illness. Birds hide symptoms until it's serious.

title: Cycle the tank first
body: A new tank needs 4–6 weeks to build beneficial bacteria. Adding fish immediately causes ammonia spikes that kill them.

title: Volume matters
body: Goldfish need 40+ liters each, a betta needs 10+ liters. Bowls are not suitable for any fish.

title: Feed in 2–3 minutes
body: Overfeeding is the #1 killer — leftover food rots and spikes ammonia. Feed 1–2 times a day, skip one day per week.

title: Water changes weekly
body: Change 20–30% weekly. Test pH, ammonia, nitrite, nitrate. Any ammonia above 0 is dangerous.

title: Signs of illness
body: Clamped fins, gasping at the surface, white spots, hiding constantly. Quarantine sick fish immediately.
